notes: The owner's words: "State constitutions, I think those should uh, be uh, correct to modern day. Um, and then every part of them should be mutable or mutatable, I guess. And that adds more legislative stuff."
52 jurisdictions: the 50 states, D.C. and Puerto Rico.
question: The owner wants state constitutions correct to the present day, and every part of them mutable in play. For all 50 states, D.C. and Puerto Rico: (1) the current constitution (or D.C.'s Home Rule Act charter and Puerto Rico's constitution), with its article structure as currently amended; (2) the amendment procedures each one actually uses (legislative referral, citizen initiative, convention, commission) with their vote thresholds and timing; (3) any parts that are entrenched or harder to change than the rest, and anything a state cannot change because federal law overrides it; and (4) a structure the game can represent so any provision can be amended, added or repealed through those real procedures.
requestedBy: research intake thread, from lamontae's message of 2026-09-22T19:50Z

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: The game holds constitutional source references and some provision-level research; this intake lane did not audit how complete or current they are across 52 jurisdictions, nor whether provisions can be mutated in play.

title: Current state constitutions for all 52 jurisdictions, with every part amendable
usableAnswer: Per jurisdiction: a pointer to the current official text with its last-amended date, the article outline, every amendment route with its thresholds, and any entrenched or federally overridden provisions. A representation scheme for provisions that supports amend, add and repeal is part of a complete answer.
whyItMatters: Constitutional provisions set offices, term limits, legislative sessions and more. If they are correct and mutable, a whole class of legislation (amending the constitution) becomes playable, and other systems can read their rules from the constitution rather than from hard-coded values.
